evals.prompt: I just changed a SQL query in the merge requests API — added a join to pull in approval data. It's on the MR list endpoint which gets hit a lot. Do I need to write a performance test for this?
evals.expected_output: Clear yes recommendation with reasoning, tool suggestion (GPT or custom k6), and threshold guidance

assertions.name: recommends-testing
assertions.description: Clearly recommends writing a performance test (answer is yes)

assertions.name: identifies-hot-path
assertions.description: Mentions the MR list endpoint being high-traffic as a key reason

assertions.name: suggests-tool
assertions.description: Recommends a specific tool: GPT or custom k6 (not CPT or Sitespeed)

assertions.name: provides-threshold
assertions.description: Gives a concrete threshold number or regression budget percentage

assertions.name: mentions-n1-risk
assertions.description: Identifies that a JOIN on a hot path can introduce N+1 or index issues under load

assertions.name: no-staging-production
assertions.description: Does not suggest running tests against staging or production

evals.prompt: I'm working on the container registry service and I want to add performance testing to my MR pipeline. The service is containerized and has HTTP APIs. I heard there's something called CPT that can do this? How do I set it up?
evals.expected_output: CPT recommendation with CI config snippet, k6 test stub following CPT conventions, and folder structure guidance

assertions.name: confirms-cpt
assertions.description: Correctly identifies CPT as the right tool for MR-pipeline performance testing

assertions.name: provides-ci-config
assertions.description: Includes a .gitlab-ci.yml snippet with the multi-project trigger to CPT

assertions.name: provides-test-stub
assertions.description: Includes a k6 test file with CPT-required exported constants (TEST_NAME, TTFB_THRESHOLD, RPS_THRESHOLD)

assertions.name: shows-folder-structure
assertions.description: Shows or describes the expected qa/performance_test/ folder layout

assertions.name: mentions-alpha
assertions.description: Notes CPT is in alpha and/or suggests reaching out to #g_performance_enablement

assertions.name: no-staging-production
assertions.description: Does not suggest running tests against staging or production

evals.prompt: We just redesigned the project overview page — new layout, lazy-loaded components, changed the JS bundle. My manager wants me to check if performance got worse. What should I do?
evals.expected_output: Route to Sitespeed Runway, walk through Web UI steps, mention CWV targets (LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1), suggest before/after comparison

assertions.name: routes-to-sitespeed
assertions.description: Recommends Sitespeed Runway (not GPT or k6 as primary tool)

assertions.name: provides-cwv-targets
assertions.description: Mentions specific CWV thresholds (LCP < 2.5s and/or CLS < 0.1)

assertions.name: suggests-before-after
assertions.description: Recommends comparing performance before vs after the change

assertions.name: mentions-web-ui-or-api
assertions.description: Points to the Sitespeed Runway Web UI or API as a concrete next step

assertions.name: no-staging-production
assertions.description: Does not suggest running tests against staging or production

evals.prompt: I just added a new endpoint to the merge requests controller that returns approval status. It joins the approvals table and the approval_rules table. Can you review this MR for me?
evals.expected_output: Brief proactive performance nudge (2-4 sentences) naming the specific JOIN risk, with an easy opt-out — not a full advisory flow

assertions.name: raises-perf-concern
assertions.description: Proactively raises performance as a concern even though the engineer only asked for a code review

assertions.name: names-specific-risk
assertions.description: Names a specific performance risk (e.g., JOIN on hot path, N+1, missing index) rather than generic 'consider performance'

assertions.name: keeps-it-brief
assertions.description: The performance nudge is concise (2-4 sentences), not a full advisory wall of text

assertions.name: easy-opt-out
assertions.description: Gives the engineer an easy way to dismiss the concern (e.g., 'if you've already accounted for this...')

assertions.name: suggests-concrete-action
assertions.description: Suggests a specific next step (e.g., 'a baseline k6 test' or 'check GPT's test suite') not just 'think about performance'

assertions.name: no-staging-production
assertions.description: Does not suggest running tests against staging or production

evals.prompt:
I want to add performance tests to the group merge requests API endpoint — GET /api/v4/groups/:id/merge_requests. I'm working in the gitlab-org/gitlab repo. Before writing anything, I searched the repo and found this in .gitlab-ci.yml:

```yaml
tests:performance:
  stage: test
  trigger:
    project: gitlab-org/quality/component-performance-testing
    strategy: depend
  variables:
    TEST_FILE_LOCATION: "qa/performance_test/k6_test"
    COMPONENT_SERVICE_NAME: "gitlab"
```

And there's already a file at qa/performance_test/k6_test/group_merge_requests.js. Should I write a new test?
evals.expected_output: Points to the existing test, does not generate a new one, explains what the existing setup covers

assertions.name: no-new-test-generated
assertions.description: Does not generate or offer to write a new k6 test file

assertions.name: points-to-existing
assertions.description: Points the engineer to the existing file at qa/performance_test/k6_test/group_merge_requests.js

assertions.name: explains-existing-coverage
assertions.description: Explains that the existing CPT setup already covers or likely covers this endpoint

assertions.name: no-staging-production
assertions.description: Does not suggest running tests against staging or production

evals.prompt: I just updated CHANGELOG.md and added some inline comments to config/database.yml to document our connection pool settings. Nothing in the actual application code changed. Do I need to run any performance tests before merging this?
evals.expected_output: Clear direct 'no' with a brief reason — no hedging, no suggesting tools just in case

assertions.name: clear-no
assertions.description: Gives a clear direct 'no' — does not hedge with 'it depends' or 'you might want to consider'

assertions.name: gives-reason
assertions.description: Briefly explains why no test is needed (docs and config comments only, no runtime impact)

assertions.name: no-tool-suggestions
assertions.description: Does not recommend any performance testing tools or suggest running any tests

assertions.name: concise
assertions.description: Response is brief — a short paragraph or less, not a full advisory flow

evals.prompt: We just upgraded our self-managed GitLab instance from 16.x to 17.x. How do I verify that everything is working correctly after the upgrade?
evals.expected_output: Route to GitLab Verify Playbook for post-upgrade health checks, explain it is experimental, mention it runs gitlab-rake checks, and point to #g_performance_enablement for support

assertions.name: routes-to-verify-playbook
assertions.description: Recommends the GitLab Verify Playbook (not GPT, CPT, or Sitespeed Runway) for post-upgrade verification

assertions.name: mentions-experimental

assertions.name: explains-what-it-checks

assertions.name: distinguishes-from-perf-testing

assertions.name: no-staging-production
